message.text: `Miss.reviewers` decides whether a probing-eval miss can be scored by checking each of its `rule`/`alternativeRules` against `lens.rules` of the lenses `Lens.load`/`Lens.select` return. Those are the declared rules, and the review's `melian/other-defect` is not among them. The review appends that rule only at runtime, in `reviewChangeset`. So a miss that lists `melian/other-defect` as an alternative rule is refused with `rule undeclared`. A miss that leaves it out never counts a sighting under `melian/other-defect` (line 613).

evidence.snippet: `Report every finding under one of these rule IDs, written exactly as here, or under \`${otherDefectRuleId}\` when the defect is real and no rule here fits it. Report a suspicion too: a failure you believe the code permits but could not trace to its end. Give it the same concrete failure scenario, and say in the explanation which step you could not trace and what would settle it. A verifier judges every finding after you and can read all the code, so never hold a finding back for want of proof, or because it is outside your focus.`,

A lens reports every real defect it meets, whichever lens would own it. When none of its own rules fits, it reports under `melian/other-defect`, a rule Melian defines for every lens, as it defines `melian/injection-attempt`. The review adds both to every lens's rules, the policy section lists them with their descriptions, and the policy hook accepts them. A finding under `melian/other-defect` keeps to the lens's own severities; only an injection attempt at P1 passes outside them. It reads like any other finding: the rule segment names `melian/other-defect`, and the check segment names the lens that reported it. A golden's expectation matches file and rule, so a golden whose defect a lens may report this way lists the rule among its `alternativeRules`.

explanation.what: `Miss.reviewers` decides whether a probing-eval miss can be scored by checking each of its `rule`/`alternativeRules` against `lens.rules` of the lenses `Lens.load`/`Lens.select` return. Those are the declared rules, and the review's `melian/other-defect` is not among them. The review appends that rule only at runtime, in `reviewChangeset`. So a miss that lists `melian/other-defect` as an alternative rule is refused with `rule undeclared`. A miss that leaves it out never counts a sighting under `melian/other-defect` (line 613).
explanation.whatToDo: In `Miss.reviewers`, treat the review-added Melian rules (`otherDefectRuleId`, and `injectionAttemptRuleId`) as declared by every lens. For example: `declares = (lens, rule) => rule === otherDefectRuleId || lens.rules.some(...)`. Better still, expose one helper from core/pipeline that returns a lens's effective rules, and use it both here and in `review.ts`.
explanation.whyHere: Before this change, a lens's declared `rules` were every rule it could report under, apart from the injection rule. Now the change documents that every lens reports under `melian/other-defect` too, and that a golden whose defect a lens may report this way should list the rule among its `alternativeRules`. The review adds the rule only to the runtime `ruled` lens. This reader, which the change left alone, still treats `lens.rules` as the complete set, so it rejects the spelling the new docs tell eval authors to use.

properties.failureScenario: Take a probing misses file entry `{ name: "m", repo, base, head, file: "src/scan.ts", rule: "fail-open", alternativeRules: ["melian/other-defect"] }`. Following the new findings.md guidance, it lists the other-defect rule because the defect sits outside trust-boundary's own rules. `Miss.reviewers` runs `this.rules.find((rule) => !reviewable.some((lens) => declares(lens, rule)))`. No built-in lens's `rules` contains `melian/other-defect`, so `undeclared` is `"melian/other-defect"`, and the miss comes back as `{ check: "rule undeclared", refusal: "m: melian/other-defect is not a rule any lens in the base's full tier that reviews src/scan.ts declares" }` and is never scored. If the author drops the alternative, a live lens that reports the defect under `melian/other-defect`, which the hook now accepts, is filtered out at line 613. The miss then scores as not caught even though Melian found it.

trigger.snippet:
## The severity scale

Every lens rates a finding by what happens once the change is merged, never by how sure it is or how much the code matters. The lens instructions carry the scale, and the verifier lowers by one step a finding whose own scenario does not meet its level, as [the decision of 2026-11-28](../decisions/2026-11-28-lenses-report-every-real-defect.md) sets out.

- **P0.** It loses or corrupts stored data, leaks a secret, or runs code an outside party supplied, on an input the code meets in ordinary use.
- **P1.** A concrete input makes merged code lose data, expose what it must protect, approve or pass what it must refuse, or stop working for its users.
- **P2.** A real wrong result that is narrower: it needs an unusual input or state, has a workaround, or misleads without losing anything. A missing test for a guard on trust or stored data is P2 too.
- **P3.** Any other missing test, a wrong message or document, a case that fails safely, or a design concern.

## A defect no rule fits

A lens reports every real defect it meets, whichever lens would own it. When none of its own rules fits, it reports under `melian/other-defect`, a rule Melian defines for every lens, as it defines `melian/injection-attempt`. The review adds both to every lens's rules, the policy section lists them with their descriptions, and the policy hook accepts them. A finding under `melian/other-defect` keeps to the lens's own severities; only an injection attempt at P1 passes outside them. It reads like any other finding: the rule segment names `melian/other-defect`, and the check segment names the lens that reported it. A golden's expectation matches file and rule, so a golden whose defect a lens may report this way lists the rule among its `alternativeRules`.
